newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end higher buoyed by fund purchases.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end higher buoyed by fund purchases.

text.p: ** (1010 GMT) Bombay blue chips end with smart gains
on strong bidding by foreign funds, traders say
** Bombay 30-share index up 32.06 points, or 0.86 percent
at 3,756.17, off 3,764.21 -- intra-day high
** Foreign funds buy into Reliance and ITC, traders say
** Telecom giant Videsh Sanchar Nigam 96/97 net profit
up at 5.03 billion rupees from 4.08 billion last year
** L&T shares gain 7.0 rupees to 213.25 after results
** National Stock Exchange halts trade at 1400 after
technical snag, resumption time undecided.
Stocks at Bombay exchanges rallied for a second consecutive day on Friday, boosted by foreign fund buying in blue chips, dealers said.
Market focus was on pharmaceutical, refinery and multinational stocks, they said.
"We have seen purchases by foreign institutional investors (FII's) over the last two days," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at Lloyds Securities.
Indian premier Inder Kumar Gujral's comment on Thursday that a hike in government-set oil prices was needed helped clear some uncertainty over the price increase, market participants said.
"There are indications that the oil price hike might not be very severe," Lloyds' Vaid said.

Prime Minister Gujral told state-owned Doordarshan television in an interview that it was better that the issue of a rise in petroleum product prices was thoroughly discussed among the partners in the ruling centre-left coalition.

Last Sunday the ruling United Front's decision-making Steering Committee met to discuss measures needed to tackle the oil pool deficit but resistance by left-wing parties prevented it from reaching a consensus.
Left-wing parties in the United Front have opposed raising prices, instead favouring increasing crude oil production and cutting import duties on crude oil and petroleum products.
Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy said on Sunday that the government was unlikely to take a decision on the issue until the next committee meeting expected in 10 days' time.
The snag-hit National Stock Exchange (NSE) resumed trade at 1615 hours (1045 GMT) on Friday, dealers said. An NSE message flashed to its members said trading will continue till 1715 hours (1145 GMT).
The NSE index was trading 21.30 points at 1,059.50.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-265 9000
